room.title: Managers Juggling Several Projects
room.description: How a manager running five projects alongside the day job keeps the whole portfolio in one view — what each project needs this week, where the hours actually go, and the loose ends that would otherwise live in their head.

desks.description: Every project on one canvas: where it is, the next milestone, hours planned against hours used, and the one thing each needs from me — so switching takes minutes, not a morning.
desks.brief:
## Portfolio view — five projects, one week

**Role** Customer experience manager, Brushbox Energy · 60-person service team
**Running** 5 projects alongside the day job
**This week** 40 hours: 24 on projects, 16 on the team and day-to-day

### The rule for this desk
Every project gets one line: where it is, its next milestone, and the single thing it needs from me. If a project needs more than one thing from me, that's the signal it needs its own desk.

### Where things stand
- **Phone system migration** — testing; go-live @+12d, soft-launch call still open
- **Office move** — handover @+3d, defects list to sign
- **Complaints audit** — report to the risk committee @+3d, findings not written yet
- **Survey overhaul** — on track, three questions waiting on my approval
- **Help centre rewrite** — 26 of 40 articles done; the writer is on leave and @+15d won't hold

### This week's trade-off
The complaints audit gets the hours. The help centre gets a scope decision instead of my time.

desks.title: Open loops — every follow-up across five projects
desks.description: The loose ends from five projects in one list — decisions I owe, things I'm waiting on, follow-ups I promised — worked every Friday so nothing lives only in my head.
desks.brief:
## Open loops — five projects

**What counts as a loop** anything I've promised, anything I'm waiting on, any decision only I can make
**Reviewed** every Friday afternoon, 30 minutes, before the weekly update goes out
**Right now** 12 open · 4 decisions I owe · 4 waiting on others · oldest 14 days

### How I work the list
1. Decisions I owe first — each one is holding someone else up
2. Waiting-ons get one nudge, then go on the agenda for that project's next meeting
3. Anything older than 10 days is closed, delegated or escalated — no fourth option

### This week
The complaints audit and the phone migration hold half the list between them. Two loops are past the 10-day line: the survey tool contract (14 days; renewal due @+18d, two days before the survey pilot goes live @+20d) and the level 3 car park passes (11 days).
